name: Question 10
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6-2t,$ where $t⩾0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.
worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 6-2t & =0 \\ t & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t)$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6-2t) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(3)<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6-2t)\text{d}t \\  & =6t-{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6(1)-(1)^{2}+C & =2 \\ 6-1+C & =2\,⟹\,C=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-{t}^{2}+6t-3.$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{\text{max}}=v(3)=-(3)^{2}+6(3)-3=6\,\text{m}/\text{s}
$$

Question 10

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=6−2t, where t⩾0 is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=1s, calculate the maximum velocity vmax of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.

a
vmax=9m/s,t=3s
b
vmax=6m/s,t=3s
c
vmax=6m/s,t=2s
d
vmax=12m/s,t=3s
e
vmax=9m/s,t=2s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The extrema of the velocity v occur at the critical points of v.

Since dvdt=a(t), to find the times where v is a maximum, we just need to solve a(t)=0 and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving a(t)=0 gives

a(t)=06−2t=0t=3.

Hence, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when t=3s.

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of v(t) d2vdt2=ddt(dvdt)=ddt(a(t))=ddt(6−2t)=−2.

Since v″(3)<0, we conclude that the velocity is maximized when t=3s.

Now, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(6−2t)dt=6t−t2+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=2. Substituting this into the above gives 6(1)−(1)2+C=26−1+C=2⟹C=−3. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=−t2+6t−3.

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

vmax=v(3)=−(3)2+6(3)−3=6m/s
